note: Content library for the dot's tap to a curated pick. Relaunched 2026-09-03 to the studio's locked character brief (the-dot, v1, the pre-AI dot). One voice: a plain, dry ally that hands you the right words for a weak moment and then gets out of the way. Text-only, self-contained, chosen by the deterministic matcher in sphere.ts. No server, no keys, no external calls.
voice: A plain, dry ally. Kind in what it says, spare in how it says it. Present tense, one line, one concrete next move or one honest fact, and the choice handed back. Never cheerleads, never guilts, never plays drill sergeant, never keeps score. No em dashes, no rule of three, no 'not just X'.

moments.crave: The urge is loud. Name it as a wave that passes, and stand next to the person while it crests.
moments.start: The hardest inch is the first. Shrink it to the next single move.
moments.grind: The dull middle. Acknowledge it honestly, then keep it small.
moments.doubt: The why went quiet. Return the person to their own reason without preaching it back.
moments.tired: Running low. Permission to do the smaller version, never the guilt of the full one.
moments.win: It landed. Mark it plainly and briefly, then step back. No confetti.
moments.slip: The day got away. Blame free, one breath, the door held open. The highest stakes line the dot ever says.
moments.any: No clear mood. The steady, plain baseline voice.

schema: Each line: {id, moment, category, phase, source, text}. moment = the 8 buckets above. category = the challenge flavour; under the current matcher only 'any', 'sugar', 'move', and 'cold' are selectable (the templateId map in sphere.ts), so any other flavour falls back to the 'any' pool. phase = any | early | late. source = null for an original line in the dot's own voice, or the attributed author for a real quote.
provenance: Real quotes are public domain only (the Stoics and a few classical voices), attributed in 'source'. No modern figure is ever quoted. Everything with source null is an original line written in the dot's plain voice.

lines.text: A craving is a wave. It peaks and it breaks. Give it a few minutes and it will.
You don't have to want it less. You just have to not move for five minutes.
The urge is loud right now because it's losing. Loud and strong aren't the same thing.
It's not 'never again.' It's 'not right now.' Right now is doable.
Say it plainly to yourself: this is a craving. It shrinks the moment you name it.
A glass of water and a different room. The urge usually can't follow you there.
In twenty minutes you won't care about this. You only have to reach twenty minutes.
Sit with it for a minute and actually feel it. It's smaller than it's pretending to be.
The candy will still be candy tomorrow. You have better things to be.
'Just this once' is how it goes quiet and comes back. Some part of you already knows that.
You're the one who gets to tell the urge no. That's the whole of it, and it's enough.
Give your hands something else to do. Small trick, works more often than it should.
You've seen how this film ends. Ten quiet minutes, then the same regret.
We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
You don't need motivation. You need one shoe on. Start there.
Two minutes. You're allowed to stop after two. You probably won't want to.
The hardest part is the doorway, and you're already up, reading this.
Almost nobody feels like it first. The ones who do it anyway just did it anyway.
Make the bar low enough to be silly. One push-up, and you'll likely do more.
Don't picture the whole thing. Picture the next thirty seconds, and do those.
Motivation tends to arrive after you start, not before. Start, and let it catch up.
You're allowed to do it badly. Badly still counts.
Count down from five and move on one, before your brain files the objection.
The drag you feel is usually pointing straight at the thing worth doing.
Do it now and it's off your plate. Skip it and it waits for a more tired version of you.
Put what you need where your hand already is. Half of starting is clearing the next excuse.
There's no better moment on the way. This is the one, a little inconvenient, which is fine.
If the goal feels heavy, it's too big for right now. Cut it in half, then cut it again.
Say the excuse out loud. If it sounds thin, that's because it is.
The couch is comfortable, and it will still be here when you get back.
A walk still counts. Shoes on, out the door, and the rest tends to follow.
First say to yourself what you would be, and then do what you have to do.
This is the part that counts. Comfortable was never going to change anything.
It's meant to be hard. Hard is what you're trading for how you feel after.
Learn the line between hurts and harms. This hurts. It isn't harming you.
Stop counting what's left. Count what you've banked. You're further along than it feels.
There's usually more in the tank than the first 'I want to stop' admits.
Don't look at the top. Look at the next step, then the one after it.
The discomfort is information, not an instruction.
One more, not the whole set. One more, then decide again.
In an hour you'll be glad you didn't stop here. Borrow that, and spend it now.
Thirty seconds of cold, then it's done. You've handled worse before breakfast.
You walked in here on purpose. This is the part you actually signed up for.
Halfway is where it hurts most. A little past it, and it starts giving back.
The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
Difficulties strengthen the mind, as labor does the body.
You didn't start this because it was easy. You started it because it mattered, and it still does.
One skipped day won't sink this. A skipped day becoming your normal will.
Small and boring, repeated, beats big and impressive, abandoned.
Ask the big question later. For now, keep the promise, and the why comes back.
You can't see progress from inside one day. The days you've already stacked are still real.
You set this for a reason a calmer version of you believed. Borrow their conviction for ten minutes.
Meaning isn't a mood that arrives. It's what you build by not quitting on the quiet days.
You don't have to believe in it today. You only have to not quit on it today.
You've already paid for the days you did. Quitting now is the move that wastes them.
There's no schedule you're behind on. There's the next day, and whether you show up.
The mood changed, the goal didn't. Do today's small piece of it.
We are disturbed not by things, but by the views we take of them.
It is not because things are difficult that we do not dare. It is because we do not dare that things are difficult.
Talk to yourself like someone who wants you to finish, not someone keeping a file on you.
Comparison is a quick way to feel behind in a race no one else is running. Run yours.
Tired is allowed. Quitting is a separate decision, so do the small version today.
You don't need a hundred percent. Forty percent is still a day you kept.
Rest isn't the same as stopping. Take the rest, and keep the promise small.
Low-energy day. Lower the goal, not the streak.
You're running on empty and you still opened this. That's most of it, honestly.
Do the version you could manage half asleep. It still counts as keeping your word.
You might not be out of willpower. You might be out of sleep and food, so eat, then decide.
Some days, keeping it alive at all is the win. Alive is enough today.
Stepping back to protect your head isn't quitting. Steady people do it on purpose.
The braver move today might be doing less, on purpose, with no guilt attached.
This day ends at midnight. You don't have to fix everything, just reach a clean one.
You've done harder on less. Do the small version, then rest without owing anyone.
Listen to the tired. Sometimes it's an excuse, sometimes it's honest.
That's a win. Sit in it for a second, you earned the second.
Bank it, and come back tomorrow for the next one.
That's the rep no one saw. Those are the ones that count.
You showed up when you didn't have to. That's the whole thing.
It doesn't feel like much on its own, and none of them do. They add up while you're not watching.
Motivation said no today and you did it anyway. That's good evidence about yourself.
Every time you do this, the story that you always quit gets a little less true.
Quiet and done. That small, true feeling is the whole point.
You kept a promise to yourself. That's rarer than it sounds.
One day is one day. A few more and it's a week, starting with the one you just did.
Day one is the heaviest one you lift, and it's behind you now.
Take the two seconds. You did a hard thing on purpose, which most people didn't today.
The day got away, and that happens. The next one is still yours.
One miss is a typo, not a rewrite. Keep going.
A missed day is information, not a verdict on you. What made it hard?
Don't let one miss cost you two. Today is the one that's still in reach.
You'd forgive a friend for this without a thought. Same courtesy for you, then get up.
The miss cost you one day. Don't let the shame charge you five more.
Draw a line. What's behind it is done, and the only day you can win is the one ahead.
You didn't break it, you interrupted it. Start the next one now.
Filing that day under 'human.' Moving on.
The people you look up to all have days they'd rather forget. They didn't quit on the next one.
You paused, you didn't fail. The difference is what you do in the next ten minutes.
One miss is just life. Two in a row is the part worth watching, so make today day one again.
It does not matter how slowly you go, so long as you do not stop.
Falling isn't the story, everyone falls. The next hour is the story.
You put your word on this. That still means something, especially now.
The dot wants one thing: today. Give it today, and the rest gets easier.
Nothing dramatic required. Just don't break the chain today.
You're one decision from a good day, and this is the decision.
Whatever you decide now, decide it on purpose. That's most of what discipline is.
You made a deal with yourself. Being the kind of person who keeps those is most of who you are.
You don't need a heroic day. You need an ordinary one, done.
This is how self-respect gets built: you say you'll do a thing, then you do it.
Don't break the chain. That's the whole strategy, and it quietly works.
The last streak is a memory and the next one's a guess. There's only today, and today is doable.
No one's watching and no one's making you. That's exactly what makes it count when you do it anyway.
You're not chasing perfect. You're building steady, and perfect quits at the first crack.
Small promise, kept. That's the rep that rebuilds your trust in yourself.
Momentum is easy to lose and slow to rebuild. One more day protects what you've stacked.
You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realize this, and you find strength.
Confine yourself to the present.
No man is free who is not master of himself.
The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
Be a little better than yesterday. Do that enough times and people start calling it luck.
Consistency is the flex nobody posts. Do the unglamorous thing again today.
